M/s SAHYADRI AUTO COMPONENTS PRIVATE LIMITED

Attention: The Managing Director and the Head - Human Resources

LEGAL NOTICE FOR ILLEGAL TERMINATION OF SERVICES WITHOUT NOTICE AND IN VIOLATION OF SECTION 25F OF THE INDUSTRIAL DISPUTES ACT, 1947

Sir,

I am instructed by and write on behalf of my client, Mr. RAMESH DATTATRAY GAWADE, aged 38 years, residing at Room No. 4, Siddheshwar Chawl, Mahalunge Village, Chakan, Pune 410501 (hereinafter "my client"), to give you the following notice.

1. That my client was appointed by you as a Machine Operator (CNC) in your Chakan factory with effect from 4 February 2019, under appointment letter No. SAC/HR/2019/041, and had been in your continuous service for more than seven (7) years and seven (7) months till the date of his illegal termination. His last drawn wages were Rs 28,500/- (Rupees Twenty-Eight Thousand Five Hundred only) per month (basic, dearness allowance and special allowance), apart from provident fund contribution and ESI benefits.

2. That my client is a "workman" within the meaning of Section 2(s) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (the "Act"), employed to do manual and technical work for hire, and you are an "industry" within Section 2(j) of the Act, a factory registered under the Factories Act, 1948, employing more than fifty (50) workmen.

3. That my client has an unblemished service record, with no charge-sheet or warning ever issued to him, and received an appreciation award on 15 August 2024.

4. That on 30 September 2026, when my client reported for duty for the first shift at 7:00 a.m., your Production Manager Mr. Vilas Kakade orally informed my client at the gate that his services were "no longer required" and that he should not come to the factory from the next day. My client was not given any written order of termination, reasons, charge-sheet, show-cause notice, or an opportunity to explain, and no domestic enquiry was held. He was not given one (1) month's notice or wages in lieu thereof, and no retrenchment compensation was paid or tendered to him at the time of such termination. His entry to the factory has since then been prevented by the security staff.

5. That the termination of my client's services by you amounts to "retrenchment" within the meaning of Section 2(oo) of the Act, and since you have not complied with the mandatory conditions precedent to a valid retrenchment as stated in Section 25F of the Act, namely, (a) one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment or wages in lieu of such notice, (b) payment of retrenchment compensation equivalent to fifteen (15) days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service or any part thereof in excess of six months, and (c) service of notice on the appropriate Government, the said retrenchment is void ab initio, illegal and invalid, and is non est in the eyes of law. You have also violated Section 25G by retaining juniors while retrenching my client.

6. That my client has been told that the real reason for the termination is that he refused to sign a blank resignation letter and complained to the Provident Fund office on 11 September 2026 about non-deposit of employer's contribution for the months of April to June 2026. The termination is, therefore, an act of victimisation and an unfair labour practice within the meaning of Section 2(ra) read with the Fifth Schedule of the Act (Item 5, discharge or dismissal by way of victimisation), and also violates the provisions of Section 33 of the Act in view of the pending conciliation on the workmen's demand dated 25 August 2026.

7. That the dues of my client are as follows:

(a) Wages in lieu of one month's notice: Rs 28,500
(b) Retrenchment compensation under Section 25F(b): fifteen days' average pay for eight (8) completed years of service (7 years and 7 months, being rounded up for the part exceeding six months), i.e. Rs 28,500 x 15/26 x 8 = Rs 1,31,538
(c) Gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, for seven (7) completed years of service: Rs 28,500 x 15/26 x 7 = Rs 1,15,096
(d) Leave encashment for 21 days of accrued earned leave (Rs 28,500 / 26 x 21): Rs 23,019
(e) Unpaid overtime allowance for April to August 2026: Rs 19,400

The total of the above is Rs 3,17,553/- (Rupees Three Lakh Seventeen Thousand Five Hundred Fifty-Three only), without prejudice to the claim of reinstatement and full back wages as stated below.

8. That my client demands that you reinstate him in service in the same position with full back wages, continuity of service and all consequential benefits from 1 October 2026 till the date of reinstatement, being Rs 28,500/- per month, and pay him the above dues, and withdraw the illegal termination order, within fifteen (15) days of the receipt of this notice, that is, on or before 29 October 2026.

9. That if you fail to comply within the stipulated period, my client shall raise an industrial dispute before the Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Pune, under Section 12 of the Act, seek a reference to the Labour Court under Sections 10 and 2A, and apply under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 before the Controlling Authority, seeking reinstatement, back wages, interest and costs, at your risk as to consequences.

10. That you shall preserve the attendance and wage registers and the gate CCTV footage of 30 September 2026. This notice is without prejudice to the other rights of my client.

Yours faithfully,

(Anil B. Shinde)
Advocate for Mr. Ramesh Dattatray Gawade
Enrolment No. MAH/2345/2012

Copy to: Assistant Commissioner of Labour, Pune.
